verses.text: When it was all over, the Israelites who'd been there went out into Judah's cities. They smashed the sacred pillars, chopped down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and altars across Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and Manasseh too. Once they'd destroyed them all, everyone went home to their own property in their own city.

Hezekiah put the priests and Levites into teams, with each person assigned a job. They handled burnt offerings and peace offerings, served, gave thanks, and praised God at the gates of the LORD’s camp.
The king set aside some of his own wealth to cover the morning and evening burnt offerings and those for Sabbaths, new moons, and scheduled festivals, just as the LORD’s law says.
He told the people of Jerusalem to give the priests and Levites their share so they could devote themselves to the LORD’s law.

As soon as the word got out, the Israelites brought loads of the first grain, new wine, oil, honey, and everything else the fields produced. They brought a tenth of everything, and there was plenty of it.
The Israelites and Judeans living in Judah’s cities brought a tenth of their cattle and sheep and a tenth of the things set apart for the LORD their God. They stacked it all in piles.
They started those piles in the third month and finished in the seventh.
When Hezekiah and his officials saw the piles, they blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the piles.

Azariah, the chief priest from Zadok’s family, answered, “Ever since people started bringing offerings into the LORD’s house, we’ve had plenty to eat and loads left over. The LORD has blessed his people, and what you see here is what’s left.”
Hezekiah told them to get rooms ready in the LORD’s house, and they did.
They faithfully brought in the offerings, the tenths, and the things set apart for God. Conaniah the Levite was in charge, with his brother Shimei as his second.

King Hezekiah and Azariah, who ran God’s house, appointed Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah as supervisors under Conaniah and his brother Shimei.
Kore son of Imnah was a Levite and guarded the east gate. He took charge of the gifts people freely brought to God and handed out the LORD’s offerings and the most holy things.

Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah worked under Kore in the priests’ cities. They were trusted to give their fellow priests their shares by team, whether they ranked high or low.
That was in addition to the males three and older listed in the family records, everyone who went into the LORD’s house for their team’s assigned service each day.
The priests were listed by their ancestral families, and the Levites aged twenty and older were listed by their duties and teams.
The family records included their little ones, wives, sons, and daughters throughout the community. Those entrusted with the work faithfully kept themselves holy.

For Aaron’s descendants, the priests living out on the pasturelands around their towns, every city had men assigned by name to give shares to every male among the priests and every Levite listed in the family records.
Hezekiah put all this into practice throughout Judah. He did what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.
In everything he started, whether serving in God’s house or following the law and commands, he was seeking his God. He put his whole heart into it and succeeded.
